A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WDPO/KLDPO research despite the expanded title. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix E report original GPT-2 emotion-alignment experiments, reward-model evaluation, preference-shift results, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendices E–F report retained emotion experiments and new LLaMA experiments using HelpSteer2, ArmoRM, and OpenLLM Leaderboard evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 reverses KLDPO weighting from exp((mean loss − loss)/tau) to exp((loss − mean loss)/tau), changing which examples receive greater weight. Appendix F additionally introduces a squared-gradient WDPO surrogate and cross-worker loss gathering for distributed KLDPO training. These change the specified procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds HelpSteer2/ArmoRM alignment with multiple preference objectives and OpenLLM Leaderboard v2 evaluation across 39 subtasks covering instruction following, reasoning, mathematics, and knowledge. Binary Emotion alignment remains, but v1's five-emotion-mixture-to-individual-emotion evaluation is removed.

E2.justification: Dr. DPO, evaluated in v1 Figures 3, 4, 8, and 9, disappears from v2's reported comparisons, removing the only external robust DPO comparator. DPO remains, and v2 Table 1 adds an explicit SFT baseline comparison. Newly cited methods such as beta-DPO are not evaluated.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 1B/3B/8B LLaMA settings, ten-response best/worst preference construction, leaderboard evaluation, and early-stopping controls. Emotion SFT and preference training now report Adam instead of RMSProp; this does not establish rerunning. V2's two-/four-epoch evaluation descriptions and Appendix F's eight-epoch training description leave exact budgets unclear.

E4.justification: V2 adds ArmoRM evaluations on unseen objectives, reward-mixture shifts, and DPO training-duration/early-stopping analyses. It removes v1's emotion correlation heatmaps, multi-class emotion robustness study, and broad nominal-mixture sweeps. The binary Emotion robustness-parameter sensitivity plots are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional plots and tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds ArmoRM results and leaderboard scores, including detailed subtask tables. For example, v2 Table 1 reports 8B MATH scores of 0.03 for DPO and 0.24 for KLDPO with tau=0.005. These are new comparisons, not v1-to-v2 performance gains. Dr. DPO results and several emotion-analysis results are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix D revises Theorem 3, its KKT derivation, and Proposition 4 from a loss-minimization calculation to loss maximization, correcting the exponential tilt and dual-variable bound. Appendix F adds a squared-gradient upper-bound argument conditional on x≥1. The main assumptions, convergence rates, and most other proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain distributionally robust DPO, two tractable algorithms, O(n^-1/4) parameter-convergence guarantees, and robustness to preference shift. V2's introduction adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first unified mathematical and algorithmic framework for addressing preference shift through distributionally robust optimization.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning restrictive data coverage and WDPO's additional gradient-computation cost. Appendix E.2 acknowledges underperformance on some subtasks and explains omitting 8B WDPO results. V1's discussion of diminishing robustness advantages when emotion preferences nearly match is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, distributed implementation instructions, and LLaMA details including eight H100 GPUs, bfloat16, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, batch size 128, scheduling, and response-generation settings. Much existing Emotion documentation moves from v1 Appendix E and its implementation table into v2 Appendix F.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of beta-DPO and concurrent Mandal et al. (2025), contrasting TV uncertainty sets and optimization-convergence guarantees with its own formulation and parameter guarantees. It also adds references supporting the new datasets, reward model, evaluation tools, and training infrastructure; the existing related-work positioning largely remains.

P1.justification: The title expands, introduction and contribution passages are rewritten, and Section 7 is reorganized into experimental setup and results. The experimental appendix is substantially rewritten and divided into results and implementation sections, followed by new limitations and impact sections. This substantially changes the narrative organization.

P2.justification: Sensitivity panels from v1 Figures 3–4 are combined into v2 Figure 2. The introductory empirical preview, multi-class emotion radar, correlation heatmaps, and extended emotion sweeps are removed. New ArmoRM plots and shaded leaderboard tables substantially replace the empirical presentation, including detailed appendix tables.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects a central inconsistency between KLDPO's worst-case objective and its stated weighting rule and proof. LLaMA evaluations substantially strengthen practical validation beyond v1's GPT-2 emotion setting, supported by distributed implementation details and explicit limitations. Removing Dr. DPO comparisons and leaving training-budget descriptions unresolved weaken the evidence, but the central correction and broader validation support a substantial net improvement.
